title: States of Matter
source: Science G3 B2 Study sheet pp.46-49; Worksheet Q4-Q6

scenes.t: Matter is anything that takes up space. Matter can be a solid, a liquid or a gas.
Matter can change from one state to another by heating or cooling.
Melting is when a solid changes into a liquid by heating. Chocolate melts in the hot sun!
Evaporation is when a liquid changes into a gas by heating. Water becomes water vapour.
Freezing is when a liquid changes into a solid by cooling. Water in the freezer becomes ice.
Condensation is when a gas changes into a liquid by cooling. Water vapour becomes water drops.
In winter we see drops of water on the windows. Warm air meets the cold glass, cools down and forms water droplets. That is condensation!
The air we blow into a balloon is a gas. Gases spread out to fill their container.

activities.title: Memory: Change of State
activities.prompt: Match each change with its name.

activities.title: Solid, Liquid or Gas?
activities.prompt: What state of matter is it?

why.l: It flows and takes the shape of its container.
why.g: It spreads out to fill any space.

activities.title: Heating or Cooling?
activities.prompt: Does this change need heating or cooling?

activities.title: Ice Cube Race & Cold Glass
need: a glass of very cold water with ice

predict.q: Which ice cube will melt first?

steps.t: Put one ice cube on a plate in a sunny or warm place, one in the shade, and one in the fridge.
Check them every 10 minutes. Which one turns to water first?
Now fill a dry glass with ice and cold water. Wait 5 minutes.
Touch the outside of the glass. Is it wet? Where did the water come from?

activities.result: The ice in the warm place melts first. Water drops appear on the outside of the cold glass.
activities.why: Heating melts the solid ice into liquid water. Water vapour in the air cools on the cold glass and condenses into drops.
